source.paraphrase: Source dependencies point inward. Entities do not mention use cases, interface adapters, or frameworks.

invariants.why: An entity that names a use case or a framework cannot move to another application without dragging that outer ring along.
invariants.fixHint: Keep the entity on its own types. Let the use case call the entity, and let the adapter implement a port the use case declared.
invariants.avoid: A type-only import or import() of the outer ring is the same dependency.

source.locator: ch. 20-22, use cases and the dependency rule
source.paraphrase: Use cases orchestrate entities. They do not import the web, the database, or a framework. Those details implement interfaces the use case owns.

invariants.why: A use case that names a web framework or a database client can only run where that detail runs.
invariants.fixHint: Accept a port (repository, clock, gateway) as an argument. Implement the port in the adapter ring.
invariants.avoid: Importing the detail through a barrel that still resolves to adapters/ or infra/ keeps the edge.

source.locator: ch. 22, The Clean Architecture (Interface Adapters; Frameworks and Drivers)
source.paraphrase: Interface adapters convert data between the use cases and the outside world. The frameworks and drivers ring is the outermost circle: it depends on the adapters, never the reverse.

invariants.why: An adapter that imports the web or database glue in frameworks/ can only be built and tested with that glue present, so swapping the framework means rewriting the adapters too.
invariants.fixHint: Let the frameworks ring call the controller or gateway and pass in what it needs. Declare the interface the adapter needs next to the adapter and implement it in frameworks/.
invariants.avoid: A type-only import or import() of frameworks/ is the same dependency. Only folder segments named frameworks or frameworks-and-drivers are matched; package imports such as express belong to CA-DEP-002 when it is selected.
